answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake, then slash it when auditors prove coordinated fraud, such as accounts submitting cloned work. Voting weight grows only with stake and time, so a swarm of fresh names cannot instantly control decisions. A knoll, hollow, or willow may label an audit task, but the labels do not prove personhood. The attacker must fund every identity and risks losing its stake, making fake identities costly to create and maintain.
